# Capability parity: UI baseline, API, CLI and MCP

The UI is the baseline for user outcomes. Maintain and deliver coverage in this order: **API → CLI → MCP**. Complete CLI work before MCP work; implement shared API prerequisites first.

The inventory contains **129 capability groups and 222 API operations**. It classifies 51 CLI command spellings, 195 MCP tools and 5 native MCP handlers. Availability is not proof of equivalent behavior.

Canonical record: [capability-parity.json](capability-parity.json). Last reviewed: 2026-09-30. Evidence: **source inventory with scoped contract/runtime evidence; real-host acceptance unverified; deployment evidence recorded separately**. Implementation and verification ledger: [CAPABILITY_PARITY_IMPLEMENTATION.md](CAPABILITY_PARITY_IMPLEMENTATION.md).

## Baseline and meaning of parity

The product target is the same authorized application outcomes across UI, API, CLI and MCP. Remote ChatGPT and Claude connections are included. A read-only connector is an implementation stage, not the final capability boundary.

- Initial audit base: `3ab55b5da86bef5e3f6864657445b9f0ba38288d`, including the preserved MCP OAuth connector. The initial integration checked main at `8468ae9f`. Collections PR #124 landed at `6905bf690cd0b9108fc74a392f51909c9726aeb2` with the same tree as tested merge `c2bd1e71d7bb6118f79ad1f07f28ae6d022a27e6`. The final Node 22/24 matrix and CodeQL passed; [retained verification and separate phase-1 staging evidence](BETA18_RELEASE_DELIVERY.md) record their proof limits.
- Current cell provenance is recorded individually. Existing connector test evidence is in [MCP delivery evidence](MCP_CONNECTIONS_DELIVERY.md). Static inventory checks do not replace cross-surface scenarios or real host acceptance.

The API and its domain services remain the state and authorization authority. Adapters must not create a second ACL or a more permissive mutation path.

`effective action = user permissions ∩ resource policy ∩ credential scopes/consent ∩ required assurance ∩ instance availability`

- Preserve owner/member boundaries, lifecycle restrictions, MFA, resource visibility, exact artifact identity, revisions, idempotency and audit attribution.
- Authentication, factor enrollment and secrets require trusted user controls. A browser handoff must report a resumable outcome; a described URL alone is not a completed workflow.
- Remote MCP filesystem changes require an enrolled local executor or explicit CLI handoff with status and receipts. A queued operation, filesystem delivery and host recognition are separate outcomes.
- Mechanism-specific transport/configuration rows may use N with a reason. This must not hide an otherwise authorized application outcome.


## Status and evidence

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| A | Operation exposed in inspected source; policy/configuration still apply |
| P | Partial outcome, parameters, lifecycle or response coverage |
| M | Missing reachable operation or blocked path |
| B | Explicit handoff/broker; destination/runtime completion not proven by this audit |
| N | Mechanism-specific; reason recorded, not a product-parity exemption |

Every surface cell has an evidence record in the JSON: source, contract test, runtime, host or deployment. Source-only availability must remain distinct from tested parity. Partial, missing, handoff and mechanism-specific cells must state their reason. MCP API-token and OAuth paths are tracked separately.

## Permission and credential boundaries

| Boundary | Current source behavior | Required proof / remaining limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scope contract | [31 application scopes](../packages/core/src/delegated-actions.ts#L24); API tokens additionally support the separate `targets:execute` scope. Existing credentials gain no new scopes. | Scope names do not prove user permission or a completed workflow; test positive and negative policy outcomes. |
| Named actions | [173 named application/public operations](../packages/core/src/delegated-actions.ts#L98) map fixed routes and required scopes. Domain services still enforce roles, resources and lifecycle. | No arbitrary HTTP proxy. API-token and OAuth credential paths need independent denial and mutation proof. |
| OAuth assurance | [Actual session MFA provenance](../apps/api/src/auth/service.ts#L763) is checked against a 15-minute privileged window; refreshing does not extend assurance. Legacy read grants retain their prior role ceiling. | Stale/missing assurance requires browser MFA and renewed consent. Current account status, roles and membership are rechecked. |
| Trusted account controls | Passwords, enrollment/recovery secrets and credential issuance remain in trusted browser/private CLI controls. Safe metadata and authorized revocation have named actions. | Handoff guidance returns no completion claim. Secret-bearing inputs must never pass through model tools. |
| Producer/executor boundary | Target observations/health and improvement execution events come from real local producers. `targets:execute` remains a local executor credential. | MCP can guide, schedule and inspect; it cannot fabricate local state, evaluator results, leases or receipts. |
| Consent and discovery | Scope effect metadata labels writes; the API-token chooser defaults only to `skills:read`. Tool visibility does not grant its advertised scopes. | Reconnect/approve scopes as needed; verify each action at call time and read resulting API state. |
| Feature availability | `/v1/capabilities` describes configured features, not effective permission for a particular user/resource. | SYS-02 is a separate product gap across all surfaces. |

These groups describe remaining work. A group can contain completed and open cells; its status comes from the individual evidence records. Delivery priority is API, CLI, then MCP.

<a id="g00"></a>

## Acceptance criteria

Before implementation, write the failure scenarios and end-to-end acceptance case for the selected capability. Use a medium-complexity workflow: two users, a team/organization resource, a scoped connector, at least two resource revisions, and a state change while the workflow is in progress.

| Proof | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Positive parity | With equivalent permission and assurance, each supported surface produces the same authorized outcome and inspectable API state. Handoffs have explicit completion evidence. |
| Negative parity | Another user, wrong team/organization, insufficient scope, stale/revoked grant, disabled account and missing MFA cannot perform the action or disclose hidden resources. |
| Fresh authorization | Change role/membership, sharing, lifecycle or consent after discovery; the next action rechecks and responds consistently. Cached tool discovery is not permission. |
| Mutation integrity | A stale revision fails safely; retries preserve the mutation/idempotency identity; a duplicate does not cause a second logical mutation; partial failures are inspectable. |
| Artifact integrity | Inspection, approval, adoption, download and installation refer to the same exact version/digest. Tampered or revoked artifacts fail closed. |
| Parameters and results | Compare required/optional fields, filters, pagination, error codes and readable results. An operation name match alone is insufficient. |
| Audit | Record acting user, delegated client/grant where relevant, resource/action, decision and outcome without secrets. |
| Local execution | Target/root binding, consent, generation, lease/fencing and receipt are verified. Distinguish filesystem delivery from recognition by the host. |
| Repeatable evidence | Save sanitized E2E results and a reproducible scenario at the tested revision. Record source, local runtime, real-host and deployment proof separately. |

Stop a slice when its approved capability rows and acceptance cases are complete. Surface unrelated findings separately. Do not bypass existing session/MFA/consent protections simply to turn a cell green.


## Maintenance workflow

1. Update the canonical JSON in every change that adds, removes or changes an application action, route, CLI command, screen, tool, permission requirement or handoff. Retain stable capability IDs; split rows when sub-operations have different coverage.
2. Classify each API method/path, CLI command spelling, MCP tool/action and native handler. Update its cell, reason, source and evidence. Keep UI as the outcome baseline; an API-only capability can also expose a UI gap.
3. Record the tested command/scenario and result in evidence when changing an availability claim. Keep missing/partial/handoff cells until their stated gap is resolved. The renderer never promotes statuses.
4. Run `npm run docs:parity -- --refresh-sources` to reconcile registered-source locations and regenerate this matrix. Changed or ambiguous cell anchors require inspection. Then run `npm run check:parity` and the affected workflow checks.
5. Review request fields, pagination, lifecycle, output, errors, permissions and resulting state. The AST drift check detects unclassified/removed registrations and stale rendering; it does not prove parameter, authorization or semantic parity. CLI subcommands, UI reachability and conditionally advertised tools still require review and runtime checks.
6. Keep real ChatGPT/Claude acceptance and deployment evidence separate. Do not turn a cell green because a model announced a change, a tool was advertised, or an endpoint returned a health response.

The required repository check fails for unclassified/removed API routes, CLI command spellings, MCP tools/actions or native handlers; invalid capability references/statuses; missing reasons/provenance; and a stale generated matrix. Unsupported dynamic registration syntax fails closed and must be made statically inspectable or added to the extractor with a failing control.

## Audit limits

- Source-level core operation inventory; not exhaustive input/output field parity or runtime acceptance.
- A status does not certify permission parity across credential kinds.
- No production deployment or real ChatGPT/Claude host acceptance in this audit.
- All registered business API routes are mapped, including dynamically registered profile/suite routes and OAuth scope routes.
- MCP request body ceiling is 14 MiB plus a 64 KiB JSON-RPC envelope; metadata responses are bounded to 512 KiB and exports to 10 MiB. These transport limits are not domain or real-host acceptance proof.
